1	# UAT 02-01 runbook: the package review on two machines
2	
3	Every command below is for you to run. `pc1` is the source, `pc2` the target; every title, answer and message prints those two hostnames, and "source" or "target" naming a machine anywhere you read is a finding.
4	
5	## 1. Machines
6	
7	Acquire the Hetzner label lock yourself and release it yourself; never run `lock.sh clear`.
8	
9	```bash
10	cd /home/janfr/dev/pc-switcher
11	export HCLOUD_TOKEN="$(pass show dev/pc-switcher/testing/hcloud_token_rw)"
12	tests/integration/scripts/internal/lock.sh status
13	tests/integration/scripts/internal/lock.sh acquire "janfr-uat-02-01"
14	export PC1="$(hcloud server ip pc1)"
15	export PC2="$(hcloud server ip pc2)"
16	for h in "$PC1" "$PC2"; do
17	  ssh testuser@"$h" 'curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flaksit/pc-switcher/refs/heads/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --ref gsd/phase-02-package-management-sync'
18	done
19	ssh testuser@"$PC1" 'bash -s -- --with-app' < tests/integration/scripts/internal/vm-test-fixtures.sh
20	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'bash -s' < tests/integration/scripts/internal/vm-test-fixtures.sh
21	ssh testuser@"$PC1" '~/.local/bin/pc-switcher init --force'
22	ssh testuser@"$PC1" 'printf "logging:\n  file: DEBUG\nsync_jobs:\n  apt_sync: true\n  snap_sync: true\n  flatpak_sync: true\n  manual_installs_sync: true\n  folder_sync: true\nfolder_sync:\n  folders:\n    - path: /home\n      enabled: true\n      filter_file: ~/.config/pc-switcher/home.filter\n" > ~/.config/pc-switcher/config.yaml'
23	```
24	
25	`init` is run for the two starter filter files it ships, and the config it writes is replaced on the next line. `/home` is the mirrored folder because both files this runbook watches the boundary at live under it — `~/.config/pc-switcher` and `~/snap` — and `home.filter` is what keeps each machine's own `authorized_keys`: a mirror of pc1's would lock the sync out of pc2.
26	
27	## 2. Diverge the two machines
28	
29	On pc1, the hold on `sl` is a hold on a package pc1 has, so it travels with the install and is never a question. The four filesystem fixtures are one scan case each: `/opt/pcsw-uat-app` holds a file, so it is the finding; `/opt/pcsw-uat-vendor` holds two directories and no file, so only you can say what it is; `/opt/pcsw-uat-empty` holds nothing anywhere beneath it; `/usr/local/share` is not scanned at all. The symlink in `/usr/local/bin` is put on both machines, so pc2 already holds it and it is never presented. The two `~/snap/hello` revision directories are the mirror's snap boundary: the run moves pc2 off the second revision and onto pc1's, so by the time the mirror asks pc2 which revisions it holds, pc1's is the only `hello` revision it can name.
30	
31	```bash
32	ssh -t testuser@"$PC1"
33	sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y sl cmatrix tree
34	sudo apt-mark hold sl
35	apt-cache policy sl | head -2                    # note pc1's installed version of sl
36	snap list hello                                  # note pc1's revision of hello
37	snap info hello | sed -n '/^channels:/,$p'       # pick a second revision, in parentheses, other than pc1's; pc2 is put on it below
38	mkdir -p ~/snap/hello/<pc1's revision> ~/snap/hello/<that second revision>
39	touch ~/snap/hello/<pc1's revision>/uat-converged ~/snap/hello/<that second revision>/uat-stray
40	ln -sfn <pc1's revision> ~/snap/hello/current
41	sudo mkdir -p /opt/pcsw-uat-app /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor/alpha /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor/beta /opt/pcsw-uat-empty
42	echo hi | sudo tee /opt/pcsw-uat-app/README /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor/alpha/run /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor/beta/run >/dev/null
43	sudo touch /usr/local/share/pcsw-uat-note
44	sudo ln -s /opt/pcsw-uat-app/README /usr/local/bin/pcsw-uat
45	printf 'allow *\n' > /home/testuser/uat.filter && flatpak remote-modify --user --filter=/home/testuser/uat.filter flathub
46	exit
47	```
48	
49	On pc2: recording `fortunes` as pc2's own makes it invisible to the review and protected as collateral; the filter on `flathub` is pc2's own and excludes the application pc1 has; of the two repository files pc1 does not have, one is used by nothing and one feeds everything pc2 has; and `hello` is moved off pc1's revision so the run has a revision to converge.
50	
51	```bash
52	ssh -t testuser@"$PC2"
53	sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y fortunes cowsay tree
54	sudo apt-mark manual fortunes-min
55	apt-get -s remove -y fortunes-min | grep '^Remv'    # must list fortunes-min AND fortunes
56	mkdir -p ~/.config/pc-switcher
57	printf 'machine_specific:\n  "apt:package:fortunes":\n    item_class: apt_package\n    label: fortunes\n    reason: null\n    recorded_at: "2026-07-30T00:00:00+00:00"\n' > ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml
58	sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/99-pcsw-uat.sources >/dev/null <<'EOF'
59	Enabled: no
60	Types: deb
61	URIs: https://uat:s3c'ret@packages.example.com/apt
62	Suites: noble
63	Components: main
64	EOF
65	sudo cp /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources /etc/apt/sources.list.d/99-pcsw-inuse.sources
66	sudo sed -i 's/^Types:/Enabled: no\nTypes:/' /etc/apt/sources.list.d/99-pcsw-inuse.sources
67	sudo snap remove hello-world
68	sudo snap refresh --revision=<that second revision> hello
69	flatpak remote-add --user --if-not-exists pcsw-uat https://dl.flathub.org/beta-repo/flathub-beta.flatpakrepo
70	printf 'deny *\nallow org.freedesktop.*\n' > /home/testuser/pc2.filter && flatpak remote-modify --user --filter=/home/testuser/pc2.filter flathub
71	sudo ln -s /opt/pcsw-uat-app/README /usr/local/bin/pcsw-uat   # a dangling symlink: the path is what pc2 holds
72	apt-cache policy tree                               # note the two versions
73	sudo apt-get install -y --allow-downgrades tree=<the older version from that table>
74	exit
75	```
76	
77	## 3. Three bookkeeping failures that end the run
78	
79	Each of these ends the run while planning, before anything is written, and each names the repair. The first two end it before any question; the third scans `/opt` first, so it asks the shape question below and aborts once you have answered it — that answer is not recorded and nothing follows it. They are checked one job at a time because a job's own review comes before the next job plans: enabling only the job under test is what keeps the run short. Every one of them is a `--dry-run`, so a check that does NOT abort changes nothing — walk out of the review with `<ctrl-c>` and record it as a finding.
80	
81	Each run must end with `Sync aborted: <message>` and exit code 1, and neither machine may change.
82	
83	```bash
84	# 1. A hold naming a package the machine does not have
85	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'sudo apt-mark hold sl'
86	ssh -t testuser@"$PC1"
87	printf 'logging:\n  file: DEBUG\nsync_jobs:\n  apt_sync: true\n  snap_sync: false\n  flatpak_sync: false\n  manual_installs_sync: false\n' > ~/.config/pc-switcher/config.yaml
88	pc-switcher sync pc2 --dry-run --yes --allow-first-sync
89	```
90	
91	The message must name the package and the machine, and give the `sudo apt-mark unhold sl` that clears it: `pc2 holds apt package(s) it does not have installed: sl.` Clear it before going on.
92	
93	```bash
94	exit
95	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'sudo apt-mark unhold sl'
96	
97	# 2. A source filter that hides what the source itself installed
98	ssh -t testuser@"$PC1"
99	printf 'deny *\nallow org.freedesktop.*\n' > /home/testuser/uat.filter   # narrows pc1's own flathub; an allow-only file denies nothing
100	printf 'logging:\n  file: DEBUG\nsync_jobs:\n  apt_sync: false\n  snap_sync: false\n  flatpak_sync: true\n  manual_installs_sync: false\n' > ~/.config/pc-switcher/config.yaml
101	pc-switcher sync pc2 --dry-run --yes --allow-first-sync
102	```
103	
104	The message must name all three things: the application `io.github.fragglet.sdl_sopwith/x86_64/stable`, the remote `flathub`, and the filter `/home/testuser/uat.filter` — and must offer both repairs, correcting the filter or uninstalling the application on pc1.
105	
106	```bash
107	printf 'allow *\n' > /home/testuser/uat.filter                     # back to a filter that offers it
108	
109	# 3. A snippet registry nobody can parse
110	printf 'snippets: [\n' > ~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml
111	printf 'logging:\n  file: DEBUG\nsync_jobs:\n  apt_sync: false\n  snap_sync: false\n  flatpak_sync: false\n  manual_installs_sync: true\n' > ~/.config/pc-switcher/config.yaml
112	pc-switcher sync pc2 --dry-run --yes --allow-first-sync
113	```
114	
115	First, choose "One application" for "/opt/pcsw-uat-vendor". Then abort should follow and the message must name the file and the machine — `the install-snippet registry ~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml on pc1 cannot be read as a registry` — and say to repair or delete it before starting a new sync. An absent registry is ordinary data, so deleting it is the repair here.
116	
117	```bash
118	rm ~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml
119	printf 'logging:\n  file: DEBUG\nsync_jobs:\n  apt_sync: true\n  snap_sync: true\n  flatpak_sync: true\n  manual_installs_sync: true\n  folder_sync: true\nfolder_sync:\n  folders:\n    - path: /home\n      enabled: true\n      filter_file: ~/.config/pc-switcher/home.filter\n' > ~/.config/pc-switcher/config.yaml
120	exit
121	```
122	
123	## 4. The run
124	
125	Re-pin `hello` before every run, this one and any repeat. pc2 tracks `latest/stable` and holds a revision from another channel, so snapd's own auto-refresh — four times a day — puts it back on pc1's revision and the change question disappears with the divergence:
126	
127	```bash
128	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'snap list hello; sudo snap refresh --revision=<that second revision> hello'
129	```
130	
131	```bash
132	ssh -t testuser@"$PC1"
133	env | grep PCSWITCHER_PACKAGE_REVIEW_AUTOMATION   # must print nothing
134	pc-switcher sync pc2 --dry-run --yes --allow-first-sync
135	pc-switcher sync pc2 --yes --allow-first-sync
136	```
137	
138	Add `--allow-out-of-order` if the topology check asks. The dry run shows every question and converges nothing; walk it first, then answer the real run so every outcome is provable: `cmatrix` `<x>` and `sl` left at install; the `cowsay` removal `<x>` and the `fortunes-min` removal `<y>`; the collateral question `<y>`, which is what takes `fortunes` with it; the repository deletion `<s>`; `hello-world` left at install and `hello`'s revision change left applied; `io.github.fragglet.sdl_sopwith` left at install; the shape question answered "one application" — the fixture cannot settle which reading is right and neither answer is wrong, so pick this one to keep `/opt/pcsw-uat-vendor` a single item and a single recorded entry for §6. The review that follows asks the two findings in sorted order, one screen each: `<y>` on `/opt/pcsw-uat-app`, write `sudo mkdir -p /opt/pcsw-uat-app && echo hi | sudo tee /opt/pcsw-uat-app/README` in the snippet editor, then `<x>` on `/opt/pcsw-uat-vendor`.
139	
140	## 5. What to check while answering
141	
142	The jobs run in order — apt, snap, flatpak, manual, then the folder mirror — and each one's questions come before the next one plans. The mirror asks nothing and runs last, which is what lets it read from pc2 what the package jobs left there.
143	
144	- Use a shifted key on one multi-item group first, to confirm it sets every line, then correct the lines you did not mean.
145	- Each group is one question: every item on a line, the answer it carries in a column to the right, arrows moving between lines, `<space>` cycling the focused line, `<enter>` confirming. Nothing is asked a second time.
146	- The legend's permanent answer reads `keep on pc2 for good; it is pc2's own, and will not be asked again` on a removal and `do not install on pc2 for good; it is pc1's own, and will not be asked again` on an install; a question that records nothing is the same widget with `<x>` missing.
147	- `sl` is offered for install and nothing anywhere asks about its hold: a hold travels with its package, so no group, line or legend mentions one.
148	- The report group is titled `Version differences (apt packages)` and notes ``These converge on their own: run `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade` on pc2.``
149	- The collateral question is titled `Removing fortunes-min on pc2 would remove fortunes`, and the line under that title — above the keys, not under the row — says it is protected on both grounds, naming `pc2` as the machine the mark is on. It names `fortunes` and offers three answers on one row: the act `<y>`, hinted `remove fortunes-min from pc2, so fortunes is removed as well`; `skip now` `<s>`; and `stop the sync` `<q>`, hinted `nothing more is changed on pc2; what earlier jobs already did stays done`. There is no `<x>`.
150	- Only after those screens are confirmed does `Delete apt repositories pc1 no longer has` appear — a second round, asked because of the answers you just gave. It comes one file at a time and offers `99-pcsw-uat.sources` only, its detail reading `pc2 would stop getting software from https://***@packages.example.com/apt` — the password appears nowhere. `99-pcsw-inuse.sources` is not asked about at all.
151	- `snap_sync` asks two questions, install before change — the order every job puts its groups in. `Install snap packages` offers `hello-world (latest/stable, revision <pc1's>)` and nothing else, with the ordinary three answers and its row starting at install: pc2 lost it in §2 and this question is what brings it back. Leave it applied.
152	- `Align snap package versions` follows, with two answers and no `<x>`, its act reading `align`: `hello`'s line reads `overwrites revision <pc2's> on pc2 with revision <pc1's> from pc1`, and the row starts applied rather than skipped.
153	- `flatpak_sync` asks once, `Install flatpak applications`, offering `io.github.fragglet.sdl_sopwith/x86_64/stable (2.9.0, flathub, user)` and nothing else, with the ordinary three answers and its row starting at install; leave it applied. Nothing else in that job is a question: the runtime the application needs travels with it, and no remote is ever offered — neither pc1's `flathub-beta` nor the deletion of pc2's `pcsw-uat`, which the log records instead (§6).
154	- `manual_installs_sync` asks `What is /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor on pc1?` while it is still planning, before its review: it names `alpha` and `beta`, and its two answers say what pc2 would be given either way.
155	- Its review then offers `/opt/pcsw-uat-app` and `/opt/pcsw-uat-vendor`, in that order, and nothing else — `/opt/pcsw-uat-empty`, `/usr/local/share/pcsw-uat-note` and `/usr/local/bin/pcsw-uat` are named nowhere, the last of them because pc2 already has it. Each item is asked on its own with three answers, titled `Install /opt/pcsw-uat-app on pc2?` and `Install /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor on pc2?`, and answering `<y>` opens the editor saying `(Ctrl-D to finish)`. Submit an empty body, then one of only spaces: each must be refused and the three answers offered again.
156	- Ctrl-C on any group ends the whole sync with `package review aborted at '<that group's title>' (Ctrl-C)`, exit code 1, and a terminal that still works.
157	
158	## 6. What to check afterwards
159	
160	On pc1:
161	
162	```bash
163	grep -c cmatrix ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml       # 1 — an install is recorded here
164	grep -c cowsay ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml        # 0
165	grep -c pcsw-uat-vendor ~/.config/pc-switcher/manual.decisions.yaml  # 1 — pc1 holds it, so pc1 records it
166	grep -c pcsw-uat-app ~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml     # 1 — the snippet you wrote
167	LOG=$(ls -t ~/.local/share/pc-switcher/logs/sync-*.log | head -1)
168	grep -E 'reviewed cowsay|reviewed fortunes \(report_only\)' "$LOG"   # "marked as this machine's own", then "applied"
169	grep -n -E 'apt-get.*sl=|apt-mark hold sl' "$LOG"              # pc1's exact version, then the hold, in that order
170	grep -E 'keeping repository 99-pcsw-inuse.sources' "$LOG"
171	grep -n -E 'apply the ref filter /home/testuser/uat.filter|sdl_sopwith' "$LOG" | head
172	grep -E 'delete user flatpak remote pcsw-uat' "$LOG"
173	grep -c "s3c'ret" "$LOG"                                       # 0
174	grep -c 'stdout: ' "$LOG"                                      # apt's, snap's and flatpak's own output, verbatim
175	grep -c 'send_file.*package-snippets.yaml' "$LOG"              # 1 — the job's own push, the registry's only route
176	```
177	
178	The filter line must come before any `sdl_sopwith` install: the filter is in force before anything installs from that remote, and pc2's own filter is never taken off for the install's benefit.
179	
180	On pc2:
181	
182	```bash
183	grep -c cowsay ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml    # 1 — a removal is recorded here
184	grep -c cmatrix ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml   # 0
185	dpkg-query -W -f='${Package} ${Version} ${Status}\n' sl cmatrix fortunes fortunes-min
186	apt-mark showhold                                # sl, registered after its install landed
187	snap list hello hello-world                      # hello at pc1's revision, hello-world arrived
188	flatpak remotes --user --columns=name,filter     # flathub carries uat.filter, pcsw-uat is gone
189	flatpak list --user --app --columns=application  # sopwith arrived under pc1's filter
190	ls /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ /opt /opt/pcsw-uat-app
191	ls ~/snap/hello                                  # pc1's revision and current, and no second revision directory
192	```
193	
194	`sl` is installed at pc1's version and `cmatrix` is absent; `fortunes` and `fortunes-min` are both gone, the collateral answer having taken them; both `.sources` files are still there; `/opt/pcsw-uat-app` exists with its `README`, the snippet having replayed in the run that authored it, and `/opt/pcsw-uat-vendor` does not — it is pc1's own.
195	
196	The mirror ran over `/home` after all four package jobs, and what it left is the boundary: `uat-converged` is on pc2 because pc2's own snapd ends the run on that revision, and `uat-stray` is not, because the revision it holds data for is the one this run moved pc2 off. The two `apt.decisions.yaml` checks above are the same boundary read from the other side — each machine still holds its own record, so the mirror carried neither machine's decision file to the other.
197	
198	## 7. Two runs with no terminal
199	
200	`ssh` without `-t` leaves the run no terminal, which is the only way to reach these paths. Sideload `hello-world` on pc2 first: a sideloaded snap is out of scope on both machines, so the run must neither move it nor mention it.
201	
202	The first run must report apt_sync SKIPPED — the repository deletion you left for now is still to be answered and nobody was there — snap_sync, flatpak_sync and manual_installs_sync successful with nothing left to decide, folder_sync successful, and a count of 0: no snippet registry is transferred without an answer, on the success outcome as much as the skipped one.
203	
204	Give pc2 a registry of its own first, holding one entry pc1 has never heard of and none of pc1's. With nobody to ask there is no push, so the mirror is the only thing left that could move that file — and it must not: pc2 ends the run holding its own entry and none of pc1's. The marker on pc1 is what says the mirror reached that directory at all in this run.
205	
206	```bash
207	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'cd /tmp && sudo snap download hello-world --basename=uat-hello-world && sudo snap remove hello-world && sudo snap install --dangerous /tmp/uat-hello-world.snap'
208	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'printf "snippets:\n  \"unreproducible:unowned-path:/opt/pcsw-uat-pc2\":\n    label: /opt/pcsw-uat-pc2\n    body: \"true\"\n    authored_at: \"2026-07-30T00:00:00+00:00\"\n    authored_on: pc2\n" > ~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml'
209	ssh testuser@"$PC1" 'touch ~/.config/pc-switcher/pcsw-uat-mirrored'
210	ssh testuser@"$PC1" 'pc-switcher sync pc2 --yes --allow-first-sync --allow-out-of-order'
211	ssh testuser@"$PC1" 'grep -c "send_file.*package-snippets.yaml" "$(ls -t ~/.local/share/pc-switcher/logs/sync-*.log | head -1)"'
212	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'snap list hello-world'      # still the sideloaded x-revision, and the log names it nowhere
213	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'ls ~/.config/pc-switcher'   # pcsw-uat-mirrored arrived
214	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'grep -c pcsw-uat-pc2 ~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml'   # 1
215	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'grep -c pcsw-uat-app ~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml'   # 0
216	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'sudo chmod -x /usr/bin/flatpak /usr/bin/snap'
217	ssh testuser@"$PC1" 'sudo chmod 000 /opt'
218	ssh testuser@"$PC1" 'pc-switcher sync pc2 --yes --allow-first-sync --allow-out-of-order'
219	ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'sudo chmod +x /usr/bin/flatpak /usr/bin/snap'
220	ssh testuser@"$PC1" 'sudo chmod 755 /opt'
221	```
222	
223	The second ends `Sync finished with failures:` with one line per failed job — flatpak_sync, snap_sync and manual_installs_sync — each naming the command that did not answer rather than the job alone, while apt_sync and folder_sync still reach their own outcome. `manual_installs_sync` fails on the scan of pc1's own `/opt`, which is half of a diff it now runs on both machines. The log also warns that snapd auto-refresh was not paused on the machine whose `refresh.hold` could not be read.
224	
225	## 8. Cleanup
226	
227	```bash
228	tests/integration/scripts/reset-vm.sh pc1
229	tests/integration/scripts/reset-vm.sh pc2
230	tests/integration/scripts/internal/lock.sh release "janfr-uat-02-01"
231	```
232	
233	## 9. Not exercised here
234	
235	Pin deletion; the repository-conflict and flatpak remote-conflict questions; the Ubuntu Pro gate; the snippet-registry overwrite confirmation and the credentials it withholds; an `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d` file differing on both machines, the only group whose permanent answer reads `do not update on pc2 for good`; a repository whose only remaining users are packages apt installed automatically; a repository kept because the removal that would have freed it was declined; the "one application per directory" answer to the `/opt` shape question; a hold whose package's install you declined, which is reported as declined rather than failed; a filter that cannot be copied or applied, which warns and fails the applications from that remote; and `--confirm-each-command` (test 3 of `02-UAT.md`).
236	
237	Of the folder boundary, only what the mirror must not carry is checked. What it does carry is a Phase 1 concern and no count, byte figure or deletion of the mirror's own is read here.
238	
239	The late collateral question needs a setup this runbook does not build: an install whose repository the same run writes, whose transaction also removes or moves a package pc2 protects. Its three answers, the withdrawn install that is neither applied nor failed, and the log line naming the repository left behind go with it. Record all of the above as not exercised rather than improvising a trigger.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -Eeuo pipefail
shopt -s inherit_errexit

# Source common helpers
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/internal/common.sh"

# Reset a single VM to its baseline btrfs snapshot state
# This script restores the VM to the known-good baseline created during provisioning
#
# Usage: ./reset-vm.sh <VM_HOST>
#
# Arguments:
#   VM_HOST    VM hostname (known to ssh) or IP address to reset

# Help
if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
    cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") <VM_HOST>

Reset a VM to its baseline btrfs snapshot state.

This script:
  1. Validates baseline snapshots exist
  2. Cleans up test artifacts
  3. Pre-flight check - detects/recovers from interrupted previous resets
  4. Replaces active subvolumes with baseline snapshots
  5. Reboots the VM
  6. Waits for VM to come back online
  7. Cleans up old subvolumes

Arguments:
  VM_HOST    VM hostname or IP address to reset

Environment Variables:
  PC_SWITCHER_TEST_USER    SSH user for VM access (default: testuser)

Examples:
  $(basename "$0") 192.168.1.100
  $(basename "$0") pc1

Prerequisites:
  - Baseline snapshots must exist (/.snapshots/baseline/@ and /.snapshots/baseline/@home)
  - Run provision-test-infra.sh if baseline snapshots are missing
EOF
    exit 0
fi

if [[ "$#" -ne 1 ]]; then
    echo "Error: Expected 1 argument, got $#" >&2
    echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") <VM_HOST>" >&2
    echo "Run with --help for help" >&2
    exit 1
fi

readonly VM_HOST="$1"
readonly SSH_USER="${PC_SWITCHER_TEST_USER:-testuser}"

# Acquire lock
acquire_lock "reset-vm-$VM_HOST"

# SSH connection helper
# First connection uses ssh_accept_new (test runner may have empty known_hosts)
# After first connection, key is stored and subsequent calls verify it
ssh_vm() {
    ssh_run "${SSH_USER}@${VM_HOST}" "$@"
}

log_step_prefixed "Resetting VM: $VM_HOST"
log_info_prefixed "SSH User: $SSH_USER"

# Establish SSH connection (accept new key if not in known_hosts)
# Test runner may have empty known_hosts or correct key from provisioning
log_info_prefixed "Establishing SSH connection..."
if ! ssh_accept_new "${SSH_USER}@${VM_HOST}" true; then
    log_error_prefixed "SSH connection failed for ${SSH_USER}@${VM_HOST}"
    exit 1
fi
